newsitem.title: UK: LME copper firmer, but still in range.
newsitem.headline: LME copper firmer, but still in range.

text.p: Copper drifted higher on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Friday boosted by an inventory decline, but showed no sign of breaking out of the recent price range, traders said.

Volumes were thin and the market appeared squeamish of moving into new territory ahead of the weekend. Three months copper ended the morning kerb at $2,356 per tonne, up $17 from Thursday's kerb close.
A 4,275 tonne LME stock decline, which was on the high end of expectations, was helping underpin the otherwise directionless market.
But traders said it could still re-test the nearby $2,310 support level, from which prices bounced on Thursday. On the upside $2,375 was offering resistance.
Cash/threes backwardation flared slightly with the three months price to $58/$60, up about $5 from Thursday.
Aluminium was little changed, holding just above the $1,650 support level of the past two weeks, where long speculative positions were said to lurk, along with active consumer interest.
On the upside trade selling was capping the market at around $1,690/$1,700, traders said. It finished at $1,655, compared to $1,658 on Thursday.
Zinc, which made good upside progress this week, was solidly underpinned by a 3,425-tonne stock drawdown and held onto most of its gains.
It ended $2 fimer at $1,282, just $5 away from Thursday's fresh 4-1/2 year high.
"Zinc looks good from a fundmental perspective and it's getting good interest. Frankly it could ease back to $1,230 before I would start thinking about getting worried," a trader said.

Lead meanwhile was quieter and was last indicated at $688/$690, down $5. The $700 level remained a viable target for lead, but prices needed to stay above $685 in order to avoid a sell-off, traders said.
Nickel was little changed at $8,085, up $25 from Thursday and well within its recent $8,000-$8,110 range.

The market ignored news that the chairman of Russia's Norilsk Nickel group said he did not think the plant would strike. Union leaders plan strikes on March 27 and April 2 over wage and vacation arrears.
Alloy was indicated little changed at $1,545/50, up about $5.
